title: The snotgreen sea
html_source:
The “snotgreen sea” mimics the common epithet describing the sea from The Odyssey—the “wine-dark sea.”

Sea imagery recurs throughout Joyce’s work. Here he describes to the sea as a mother. There is a constant contrast to fertility and barrenness through the tides and flux of rivers and oceans. This theme will extend into Joyce’s masterwork, Finnegans Wake. The character of Anna Livia Plurabelle who is the symbolic embodiment of womanhood and reticulation of water as she floats down the River Liffy.
